subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: What sender identity authority should OpenClaw expose as trusted inbound metadata: raw resolved display names, stable provider IDs, or configured principals such as session.identityLinks?
rationale: The current code intentionally keeps human names and per-turn identifiers out of trusted system metadata, so adding a model-visible sender identity field changes a security, privacy, and prompt-cache boundary rather than filling a purely mechanical omission.

options.title: Use Configured Principals
options.body: Expose a trusted principal only when a stable provider ID matches an operator-configured identity link, keeping raw display names in untrusted context.

options.title: Use Stable Provider IDs
options.body: Expose stable provider IDs as trusted metadata and require agents or tools to resolve human-readable names outside the prompt contract.

options.title: Use Resolved Display Names
options.body: Expose platform-resolved names directly, accepting higher privacy and spoofing-review burden for easier agent ergonomics.

recommendation.title: Use Configured Principals
recommendation.body: Expose a trusted principal only when a stable provider ID matches an operator-configured identity link, keeping raw display names in untrusted context.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties steipete to the trusted/untrusted prompt boundary and broader inbound context ownership.
